title: Nekuda, sefira, partzuf: why the essential points of Tohu break, and how Tikun makes a person
overview:
Before the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, the chapter brings in *nekuda*, *sefira* and *partzuf*: the difference between *Tohu* and *Tikun*. In *Tohu* each *sefira* is a point, the essence of an attribute before it spreads: a will for kindness that has a definition but no reason and no particular ways, like a person who is kind by nature, not one who read Dale Carnegie. Even its intellect and its *netzach* are the same point, all in one vessel, the *Akudim*.

So the *sefiros* of *Tohu* cannot join: two opposite essential goals allow no compromise, and whoever makes one of them the cure-all, "totally nice, always" or "get it yourself", fails. *Tikun* is the will for how to reach the goal. Kindness then depends on a reason, and one thing can be loved and hated at once, as G-d punished Shaul and ordered his eulogy at the same time. Only *Tikun* makes a *partzuf*, a person who sees the goal both sides share and takes the practical step, the way G-d mixed fire and water.

terms.gloss: the world of Chaos: each sefira only a point, an essential goal that cannot join its opposite
the world of Repair: each sefira divided into ten, so that they work together in harmony; the will for how to reach the goal
a point: the essence of an attribute before it spreads out, a bias with no reason and no particular ways
inclusion: the attributes working together like a harmony
the Name of forty-five: the abstract that a concrete form, BaN, comes to express
the Name of fifty-two: the concrete form, a vessel or an angel, that represents the abstract MaH
the bound ones: all ten sefiros included in one vessel, all one point
here: the point of Tohu even when divided into ten, each still a point, with no inclusion
lit. face: the stature of a person, the inclusion of all opposites; only in Tikun
composite kindness: kindness that depends on a reason, such as to one who did you a favor, weighed out by the situation
a middle: the place a thing loved from one side and hated from another ends up on one's list
a person of daas, who explains each of two opposite views better than its holder and finds the goal they share

sections.title: Before the sefiros of Atzilus: nekuda, sefira, partzuf, and the difference between Tohu and Tikun
sections.summary: Before the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are explained one by one, the chapter brings in the three stages *nekuda*, *sefira* and *partzuf*. In *Tohu* each *sefira* is only a point; in *Tikun* each is divided into ten, and so they work together in harmony, through the Name *MaH*.

phrases.he: (כ) והנה קודם שיבואר ענין פרטי העשר ספירות דאצילות יש להקדים ענין נקודה ספירה פרצוף כו'
דהיות ידוע ההפרש שבין בחינת התהו לבחינת התיקון בכלל,
דעשר ספירות דתהו הן בבחינת נקודות לבד,
phrases.en: In *Tohu*, each *sefira* is like a *nekuda*.

phrases.he: שהן בבחינת הכתרים

blocks.text: Now he starts on *Keser*. First the chapter explains *nekuda*, *sefira* and *partzuf* (point, attribute, full stature), and *Tikun* and *Tohu*, to show how the *igulim* of *Atzilus* relate to its *yosher*.

**In *Tohu*, each *sefira* is like a *nekuda***, not yet ten. Tying your *etzem ratzon* to something, as the last chapter explained, makes a leaning towards *chesed* or another way: only a point, not yet a will for anything particular, but the source of every particular after it.

phrases.he: ובעולם התיקון הוא בבחינת התחלקות כל ספירה לי',
phrases.en: And then in *Tikun*, each *sefira* becomes already divided to ten.

phrases.he: על כן ממילא נעשה בחינת התיקון
phrases.en: and since each *sefira* is now diverse, it automatically makes it *Tikun*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת ההתכללות
phrases.en: That's the idea of *hiskalelus*, that it's like a harmony.

phrases.he: על ידי שם מ''ה כו'

blocks.text: In *Tikun* each *sefira* is divided into ten, and being diverse, that makes it *Tikun*, which here means a harmony, things working together: *hiskalelus* (inclusion), **it's like a harmony**.

The harmony comes through the Name *MaH*. *MaH* and *BaN* always relate so: when something concrete with a set form, a *kli* or an angel, carries something abstract, the abstract is *MaH* and the *kli* *BaN*.

blocks.title: Letters make a vessel for an idea
blocks.text: Like language: letters, a tangible form, set in different orders make a *kli* to express an abstract idea.

sections.title: The point: the essence of a midda before it spreads, a will for kindness with no reason
sections.summary: The *nekuda* is the essence of an attribute before it spreads out. It is not the essence as it is in the *yechida*, but the will for kindness once it is revealed: it already has a definition, but no reason and no particular ways of coming out.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע שבחינת הנקודות הוא בחינת העצמיות טרם שמתפשט,
phrases.en: The *nekudos* is like the *etzem* before it spreads out,

phrases.he: כנקודה שהיא בלתי מתפשטת כו'
phrases.en: like a *nekuda* that doesn't come out yet.

blocks.text: **The *nekudos* is like the *etzem* before it spreads out.** As the *igulim* and the *yosher* are the soul before and in the body, so *Tohu* and *Tikun* are a thing in its *etzem* and spreading out: **like a *nekuda* that doesn't come out yet**, still *hiyuli*.

phrases.he: כמו אור מדת החסד,
phrases.en: for example, *chesed*,

phrases.he: הנה בחינת עצמיות דמדת החסד הוא בחינת הכתר שלו

blocks.text: Take, **for example, *chesed***: its essence, its *Keser*, is a desire for kindness, so a person always leans to doing things nicely.

phrases.he: ואמנם אין הכוונה על בחינת העצמיות דמדת החסד כמו שהוא נטוע ומושרש בעצם הנפש שנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: But we're not talking here about the *etzem* like it is in the *yechida*,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל, שהוא בחינת היולי לגמרי (כנזכר לעיל באות יו''ד וי''א)
אלא הכוונה הוא על בחינת גלוי הרצון לדבר חסד פרטי
phrases.en: We're talking about now when a person has a particular *ratzon* for doing an actual kind thing.

phrases.he: מן העלם חסד העצמיות ההיולי

blocks.text: Not *chesed* as it is rooted in the *yechida*, the essence of the soul, wholly *hiyuli*: that is before the *tzimtzum*, as chapters 10 and 11 said.

It is the will for a particular kind act, revealed from the hidden essence. The essential *chesed* made a will to be nice; *Adam Kadmon*, a picture of what nice is; and the picture yields wills to do nice things.
Yet all those acts share one *nekuda*, that he sees them as nice. Through *Adam Kadmon*, *chesed* now has a dictionary definition, but the point, wanting whatever is nice, is still there.

phrases.he: שגם זה הרצון
phrases.en: even this particular *ratzon*, that you want to do a nice thing,

phrases.he: הוא בלתי התפשטות עדיין
רק כמו שהוא בלא טעם כלל
phrases.en: this is without any reason at all,

phrases.he: לרצון זה, למה רוצה בגלוי לחסד זה כו'
ומכל שכן שאין בו בחינת התחלקות אופנים שונים
phrases.en: and he definitely didn't yet think up particular ways of exactly what he wants to do.

blocks.text: Even this will is still without *hispashtus*: he knows what being nice means, but nothing particular yet; the situation will decide. A nice person leans towards kindness, but when nothing comes up, he does nothing.
And **this is without any reason at all**: not a means to a goal in some situation. The *chesed* is the goal, his *etzem*, the *nekuda*; he likes it because of who he is.

blocks.title: Dale Carnegie's book
blocks.text: Not like someone nice to people because he read Dale Carnegie's *How to Win Friends and Influence People* and wants a career: the *nekuda* of his will is the money, not being nice.
One who by nature is *chafetz chesed* makes kindness part of his self-image and life goal, and such an *Adam Kadmon* gives him a constant *nekuda* to do kind things.
Still less is it divided into ways. Not being a means, he **definitely didn't yet think up particular ways of exactly what he wants to do**: just whatever is kind.

blocks.title: A will for money, from any deal
blocks.text: Likewise an *etzem ratzon* for money does not care which deal it comes from; it wants the money. Here he wants the *chesed*, however it comes.

sections.title: Intellect and victory inside the point: all one point, the Akudim in one vessel
sections.summary: Even the bias of the intellect towards kindness, the *chachma* of that *chesed*, and its *netzach* are only the same point. The ten are there, but with no recognizable division: this is the world of *Akudim*, all in one *kli*.

phrases.he: או גם אם שכלו מטה כלפי חסד דווקא, אין בו התחלקות אופנים שונים
אף על פי ששכל הנוטה בעצם לחסד ולזכות, הוא בחינת חכמה שבחסד העצמי, אבל גם הוא רק בבחינת נקודה

blocks.question: If his essential will biases his intellect towards kindness, is that not *chachma*, a division already within the point?
blocks.text: That too is a *nekuda*, not yet an actual *sechel*. His intellect will always lean to being liberal and kind, to a good eye, but the leaning is part of the same point, not divided into ways.

His intellect leaning to kindness and merit is the *chachma* of the essential *chesed*, but as a point. Even in *Tohu* everything divides ten within ten, so a *chachma* is there, but it is the same *nekuda*: his *chachma* and *middos* all want *chesed*, before any situation; whatever comes up, he already leans this way.

phrases.he: וכן נצח שבחסד זה
phrases.en: that he's going to want to overcome any opposition to any *chesed*.

phrases.he: הוא בא בבחינת נקודה
ונמצא דגם שבחינת החסד העצמי הבא בגלוי כלול מי', רצון ושכל ומדות, אבל אין בהם התחלקות ניכרת
phrases.en: even though really, technically, it does have ten, you could divide it up into ten *sefiros*, there's no recognizable distinction

phrases.he: אלא כולן בבחינת נקודה אחד,
phrases.en: they're all in one *nekuda*,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת העקודים, שעקודים היו בכלי אחד כו'
phrases.en: This is the level of *Akudim*, where really all of the ten *sefiros* are included in one *kli*,

blocks.text: So too its *netzach*: **that he's going to want to overcome any opposition to any *chesed***. Nothing blocks him yet, but if something did, he would fight it. This too is a point.
So the essential *chesed* coming out includes all ten, will, intellect and *middos*, with no recognizable division: technically ten *sefiros*, but one point, all going to *chesed*.

**They're all in one *nekuda***. **This is the level of *Akudim***, all ten *sefiros* in one *kli*: his will, intellect and *middos* all mean that he wants *chesed*, and it does not matter which you name. It is his final goal.

sections.title: Sefira: the sefiros of Tohu cannot join, and two opposite goals cannot compromise
sections.summary: Because each *sefira* of *Tohu* is an essential goal, they cannot unite: one reigns and dies, then the next. Two opposite essential wills cannot be mixed or compromised, and a person or a society that makes one of them the cure-all fails; so too Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel could not convince each other.

phrases.he: ולזה בחינת עשר ספירות דתהו הן בלתי מתיחדין ומתכללין זה עם זה
phrases.en: And therefore the *sefiros* of *Tohu* do not unite or include with each other at all,

phrases.he: אלא הן זה תחת זה
phrases.en: they're one under the other,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב וימלוך וימת כו'

blocks.text: So **the *sefiros* of *Tohu* do not unite or include with each other at all**: **they're one under the other**, as it says of each king of *Tohu*, the kings of Esav, "and he reigned, and he died."

phrases.he: כמו רצון העצמי שבא בגלוי חסד
הגם שכלול בו שכל כו', לא יתחבר עם רצון עצמי היפוכו הבא בבחינת הדין

blocks.text: So the essential will that comes out as *chesed*, intellect and all, will not join its opposite, which comes as *din*: as in politics, one leans liberal, another conservative, for whatever reason.
You see it in anything people believe in, as with missionaries and the like: it is really a belief, an *etzem nekuda* they are connected to, and they believe it whatever it is.

sensitivity.reason: Holds up missionaries as the type of believer whose reasoning is only a front for a fixed belief.
sensitivity.publishable: You see it in anything people believe in: it is really a belief, an *etzem nekuda* they are connected to, and they believe it whatever it is.

blocks.text: Both sides come into *sechel* to convince you, but it is really *ratzon*, their belief. Argue with such a person forever and you will never convince him; it is a one-way *sechel*: "*sechel*'s a puppet to convince you of what they believe."
Not necessarily bad; this is how it starts. At this level *sechel* just expresses to another what you believe; it cannot convince someone whose *etzem nekuda* lies elsewhere.
That is also why, whenever you come to something like this, as in Israel with the Jews and the Arabs, democracy does not work, because it is a religious thing.

sensitivity.reason: A political opinion on the conflict between Jews and Arabs in Israel and on democracy there.

blocks.text: Two people whose inner goals conflict cannot be told to compromise. On things that serve the goal they can: wanting different things, they find one to their mutual benefit and both gain. On the goal itself there is no room; one *etzem ratzon* is the exact opposite of the other.
When the issue is the thing itself, one man's life against another's, "it's an all-or-nothing deal." So too within one person: of these essential wills, only one at a time.

blocks.title: Totally nice, always
blocks.text: Some people live in *Tohu*, in the *igulim*: they lock on to *chesed* and resolve to be totally nice, always. Without a mature view, they do not see that to accomplish *chesed* you sometimes have to do something outwardly *gevura*, which is the *inyan* of *Tikun*. So they get stepped on; try it with a country or a classroom and it fails, and dies.

blocks.title: "Get it yourself"
blocks.text: Then he switches to *gevura*, also the *Tohu* way: ask him to pass the salt and he says, "Get it yourself." Making people work has a *maala*, but only giving people what they deserve fails too, and dies. A person or society that makes any one of these the cure-all fails; and only one is possible at a time, since in essence they contradict.

phrases.he: (כמחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל וכהאי גוונא,
דגם שמנגדו יקשה עליו
phrases.en: even if the opposition will ask questions to him,

phrases.he: ולא יוכל למצוא טעם
phrases.en: and he's not able to find an explanation,

phrases.he: ישתוק,
phrases.en: he'll be quiet,

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכל להודות ולחזור בו,
phrases.en: he's not able to admit and then change his mind,

phrases.he: להתכלל בדעה שמנגדו כלל כו')
phrases.en: to the opposite opinion at all.

blocks.text: Like Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel: reasonable people, why did they not convince each other? Their dispute came from the root of their souls, not from *sechel*, a *Tohu* kind of thing; but they were in holiness, so the example is in parentheses, not a full one.

Once the *halacha* was decided, each did as it went. Their essential leaning biased how they saw things, but their bond with Torah was deeper: if the Torah said so, they did it even without seeing it that way.

So **even if the opposition will ask questions to him**, and **he's not able to find an explanation, he'll be quiet**, saying he does not know; but he cannot give up his opinion: it rests not on logic but on how he perceives things, and the *sechel* only seeks words. So in Torah: they perceive it spiritually, then find words for human intellect, which is not its root.

But **he's not able to admit and then change his mind to the opposite opinion at all**: each holds an essential point, and *eilu v'eilu divrei Elokim chaim* (these and these are the words of the living G-d), so neither has reason to concede.

sections.title: Tikun: the midda spreads out of its essence, into a will for how to reach the goal
sections.summary: In *Tikun* the attribute comes out of its point: it is no longer about the goal but about how to accomplish it in a particular case. Then kindness depends on a reason, like kindness to one who did you a favor, and it is a composite kindness; so too the composite judgement of a kind man toward his enemy.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת התיקון היינו כאשר המדה בא מבחינת נקודה שלה להתפשטות חוץ מן העצמיות רצון ושכל שבה

blocks.text: *Tikun* is the *midda* coming out of its point into *hispashtus*, outside its essence, will and intellect. Leave the goal, the *etzem ratzon*, aside: now we are talking about how to accomplish it.
Your essential goal is religion, which is about ultimate truths, the ultimate reality and goal of a person and of the world; there can be only one: "you can't have pluralism in religion."

blocks.title: Going to New York by way of the south
blocks.text: The means are another matter. Traveling, you must know your destination and cannot change it: going to New York, you are not going to Chicago. But to go north you may have to go south around something, a separate will. Whoever just walks straight at it runs into all the walls in his way.

blocks.title: The short long way and the long short way
blocks.text: Two ways to the palace. The short long way goes straight and ends very close, at a wall you cannot get past: short, yet long. The long short way compromises and goes slowly, but is short, because it gets there. "Shortcuts make for long delays": clever schemes in these things are not worth it.
That is *Tikun*: not the *etzem ratzon*, but the will for how to accomplish it in a given case.

phrases.he: דהיינו כמו מדת החסד כאשר יולד הרצון ושכל להטות כלפי חסד לזולתו
מצד שעשה לו טובה
phrases.en: You want to be nice to somebody because he did you a favor.

phrases.he: ולא מצד בחינת עצם הטוב הבא בגלוי בהכרח מטבע הטוב שבעצמיות נפשו
אדרבה יוכל להיות אכזרי בטבע,
phrases.en: The person could be cruel naturally.

phrases.he: ולמי שחננו והצילו ממות
phrases.en: But to somebody that saved his life, that did a lot of kindness to him and saved his life,

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
ירצה להטיב,
phrases.en: for that person he's going to always be gracious,

phrases.he: ויטה שכלו עליו תמיד לחסד וזכות
phrases.en: and he's always going to be biased to look at them favorably.

phrases.he: כו' וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: Take *chesed* born of a favor, not of an essential wish to be kind to everyone: **you want to be nice to somebody because he did you a favor.**

Say he wants his own happiness, or money: he will be kind to the man who helps him, reasoning that it will pay off later, or out of simple gratitude. But not to everybody: he is nice to those who are nice to him, and not to those who are not.
Not the essential kindness of his nature, which would have him be nice to everybody, whatever they had done to him.

On the contrary, **the person could be cruel naturally**. **But to somebody that saved his life, that did a lot of kindness to him**, **he's going to always be gracious, and he's always going to be biased to look at them favorably**. He ties his *etzem ratzon* to that person as far as the person did for him. Now it gets complicated, when to be nice and when not: the *ratzon murkav* (composite will).

phrases.he: שזה נקרא חסד וטוב המורכב,
phrases.en: this is called a complex or composite kindness and good.

phrases.he: ולא חסד פשוט ועצמי
phrases.en: it's not the same simple thing for everybody

phrases.he: שמצד הטבע כלל
וכהאי גוונא יובן בהיפוכו,
phrases.en: the same way with the opposite,

phrases.he: במדת הדין המורכב, להטות רצונו ושכלו כלפי חוב לשונאו שעשה לו רעה הרבה,
גם שבעצם טבעו הוא איש חסדן ורחמן כו'
phrases.en: even if *b'etzem* he's a kind person,

blocks.text: This is **a complex or composite kindness and good**, *chesed hamurkav*: many parts, the situation weighed; not a simple *chesed* from nature, **not the same simple thing for everybody**.

**The same way with the opposite**, composite judgement: someone who did him much harm becomes his enemy. That does not make him cruel, **even if *b'etzem* he's a kind person**: he may like to be kind by nature, yet see there are people one should not be nice to.
Had he made *chesed* his whole *metzius*, he would be nice even if it got him killed. But at the *pnimiyus*, even *Tohu* has a head, the inner will it comes from, so *Tikun* has a higher root.

blocks.title: The parent who wants to be loved
blocks.text: A parent who wants his children's love is outwardly kind so they will love him back; he does what they will see as kind, which is not really wanting to be kind. The inner will to be kind is for their benefit, and whoever really wants that will do what outwardly looks like *gevura*, as the *sechel* decides.

sections.title: In the composite, opposites can live together: love and hate, Shaul, Shlomo and the Flood
sections.summary: Once the attributes are tied to a thing through a reason, one thing can be loved from one side and hated from another, and a middle is weighed out between them. So G-d punished and honored Shaul at once, was angry and joyful over Shlomo, and found in man's evil inclination both a reason to destroy and a reason to spare: in *Tikun*, in the actual world, nothing is pure.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יובן שיוכל להיות במורכב כמה מיני אופנים שונים
phrases.en: once you start having these considerations, it can come out in many different ways

phrases.he: מאד, לפי אופן דבר שמורכב בו המדות
phrases.en: according to the considerations that you're using to put together the *middos*.

phrases.he: כמו אהבה ושנאה
התלויים בדבר
phrases.en: that are dependent on something,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל
הרי יוכל למצוא דבר שמצדו א' יאהבנו, ויהיה רצונו ושכלו הכל לטוב וחסד, ומצדו הב' באותו הדבר עצמו, ישנאנו ויטה רצונו ושכלו לרע ועונש

blocks.text: **Once you start having these considerations, it can come out in many different ways**, as the *middos* are put together: like love and hate **that are dependent on something**, the same thing loved from one side, with will and intellect for kindness, and hated from another, leaning to punishment.
Hang your essential *middos* on something by a *sechel*, and by one consideration it is good for you, by another bad: you love it and hate it.

blocks.title: Drugs and their side effects
blocks.text: Drugs, for example: liked because they feel good, hated for their side effects. Being one thing in the world, it carries both; you cannot have one without the other.
Your *sechel* ties two opposite *middos* to the one thing, and you have to decide which wins in practice, and how to act.

phrases.he: עד שיוכל להיות בחינת ממוצע
phrases.en: until you come out with a *memutza*

phrases.he: כלול מחסד וגבורה יחד

blocks.text: **Until you come out with a *memutza***, a middle, including *chesed* and *gevura*. Essentially nothing mixes: what you like or hate, you do totally. But in practice you can prioritize, putting a thing in the middle of your list: good on one hand, bad on the other.

blocks.title: Profit and expenses in a business deal
blocks.text: In a physical thing both come together, so you can do a simple equation: weigh the pleasure against the pain, subtract, and maximize. Like a business deal: you want the profit, not the expenses. A deal may bring in money and still lose more than it gains, or gain a little, or a lot.

blocks.title: Only a deal that is profitable enough
blocks.text: The money is always what you want; but going by *sechel*, you take only a deal profitable enough to meet your needs, not any deal where somebody pays you. So you make a hierarchy, and a *memutza*: this one is so-so.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב באשר משפטו שם כו'
על שאול שהמית את הגבעונים ועל שלא נספד כהלכה,
דבר והיפוכו כאחד

blocks.text: As it is written, *ba'asher mishpato sham* (he does not recall the end of the word): where *Hashem* judges, there you find His compassion and *chesed*, seemingly opposites.

blocks.title: Shaul punished and eulogized
blocks.text: This was said of Shaul, who killed the Givonim and was not properly eulogized: one thing and its opposite at once. Because Shaul had killed the Givonim, who had helped Dovid, a plague came; prophecy showed it was for Shaul, and some of his descendants were handed to the Givonim to be hanged. At the same time Dovid was told to eulogize Shaul, who had never been given proper honor.

So is G-d angry with Shaul or pleased? He punishes and rewards him at once, because neither is essential. A parent who yells at a child for doing wrong still loves him: he likes the good and not the bad, and the two are unconnected, so both can be at once.

phrases.he: וכן כשנשא שלמה בת פרעה,
phrases.en: also with *Shlomo*, that *Hashem* was angry because he married *Bas Paroh*,

phrases.he: על זה אמר כי על אפי כו'
phrases.en: that this is: I'm angry,

phrases.he: ושיר השירים נאמר על שמחת בנין בית המקדש
וכמו שכתוב ביום שמחת לבו כו'
phrases.en: the day of the rejoicing of his heart, which is the time the *Beis HaMikdash* was built,

phrases.he: שמחה וחרון אף, דבר והיפוכו כאחד
phrases.en: So we see that *Hashem* both had *simcha* and anger at *Shlomo* at the same time.

blocks.text: So too Shlomo: *Hashem* was angry that he married *Bas Paroh*, *ki al api*, "**I'm angry**", forever. Yet *Shir HaShirim*, a song of joy and of *Hashem*'s love for Shlomo, was said on the joy of building the *Beis HaMikdash*, "on the day of the rejoicing of his heart." Joy and burning anger, at once.

phrases.he: וכן כי יצר לב האדם רע וכו'
phrases.en: and the same thing with man

phrases.he: ומתחלה אמר וירא יהו״ה כי רבה רעת האדם כו' וינחם כו'
phrases.en: First, before the flood, it says G-d saw how bad man was, and He regretted making man.

blocks.text: **And the same thing with man**: before the *Mabul*, man is bad, so destroy him; after it, man is bad, so do not. His *yetzer hara* is a reason both to hate him and to pity him.

blocks.title: Both sides of a court case
blocks.text: Like a court case, each side shows how the same *nekuda* leads to *chesed* or to *gevura*: they are born bad, so they will sin; born bad, so it is not their fault, go easy; no, born bad means there is no hope at all. It depends: "Whatever you want, you'll be able to use that as an excuse for it."

blocks.title: Why the rainbow came after the Flood
blocks.text: In the end, before the *Mabul* the bad could not be refined; after it the world was refined a little, hence the rainbow. Before, the atmosphere was too thick; after, thinner, so light came through the cloud, struck the raindrops and showed its hidden beauty through that resistance.

blocks.title: Why the rainbow came after the Flood
blocks.text: So after the *Mabul* a person's bad could be used for good: the fight to overcome his *yetzer hara*, the difficulty of doing what G-d wants, brings out the inner beauty of his *nefesh Elokis* and its bond with G-d. Before, it could not, so the bad side won.
At first, before the *Mabul*, G-d saw how bad man was, and He regretted making man.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר
שזהו מבחינת המדות דתיקון,
phrases.en: the fact that you can have both *middos* for the same thing is because it's in *Tikun*,

phrases.he: שהם בבחינת מורכבים
phrases.en: which are complex.

phrases.he: דהיינו בהתפשטות דבר
phrases.en: that you're dealing not with a theory.

phrases.he: שלא מצד העצמיות לבד
על כן יוכל להיות התכללות דבר והיפוכו כו'
phrases.en: Therefore, you can have two opposite things,

blocks.text: As a *maamar* explains, **the fact that you can have both *middos* for the same thing is because it's in *Tikun***, where they are composite, in the thing's *hispashtus*. In theory things are pure; in practice nothing physical is wholly pleasure or wholly pain.

blocks.title: All the powers of the soul in one body
blocks.text: In the physical world everything comes together, as the soul in the body: sight, hearing and all its powers meet in one body. So any physical thing holds all the *sefiros* and *middos* in different proportions, never just itself.

blocks.title: No light without a little darkness
blocks.text: **Therefore, you can have two opposite things.** In theory light and darkness, sweet and bitter, are complete opposites; in practice everything is a mixture. No light is so pure it could not be brighter, so there is a little darkness in it.

sections.title: Tohu stays a sefira; only Tikun makes a partzuf, a person, like fire and water mixed
sections.summary: Even divided into ten, the point of *Tohu* is only a *sefira*, not the *partzuf* of a person who includes all opposites. A person, and *Tikun*, sees the deeper goal both sides share and works it out in practice, without dropping the goal; as *Sefer Yetzira* says, G-d mixed fire and water, not in their essence but as composites.

phrases.he: והיינו בחינת נקודה דתהו,
דגם כשנעשה בהתחלקות לי', אין זה רק ספירה
phrases.en: Even in *Tohu*, when it divides up into a *sefira*, and it has ten *sefiros*, they're also *nekudos*.

blocks.text: The point of *Tohu*, the essential *middos*, is *Akudim*, one point. **Even in *Tohu*, when it divides up into a *sefira*, and it has ten *sefiros*, they're also *nekudos***, not real *hiskalelus*: the *chesed* takes the *gevura* and makes it *chesed* too.

blocks.title: Even more reason to be nice to him
blocks.text: Like those who lean to *chesed*: tell them all the bad a man did, and it is more reason to be nice to the poor victim. They turn anything into *chesed*.

Because it is a *sefira*: a man who in his essence believes or wants a certain way, from faith or will. He may even go out to missionize, like the *Akudim*, but it is one *sefira*: he does not consider the other side at all.

The sign of it: a person in the way of *Tohu* makes his whole *partzuf* of one *sefira*. The real *etzem* includes all ten and should hold them together; one who cannot shows a great *shtarkeit*, a fierce opposition to the opposite, because he feels it threatens his *inyan*.

*Tikun* needs a deeper look; the next chapter explains the middle *kav*, which joins opposites. The *chesed* man vehemently opposes the *gevura* view and the *gevura* man the *chesed*, each seeing the other as "completely evil and wrong and subversive."

But a *bar daas*, as the Frierdiker Rebbe describes *daas* in a *maamar*, offers to explain each one's view to him better than he understands it himself. He peels it down to its depth: you do not really want a particular instance of *chesed*, but the *etzem ratzon* of *chesed*, before it is tied to a deed. He brings it up a step.

Up a step, you ask why you really want *chesed*. Every person has a little good in him; you lean towards letting him off because you value that good and want to bring it out, to help him and others. That is the main *nekuda*.

*Gevura* answers that what is inside, good intentions or potential, is worthless if it does not come out in deed. So both want the same thing, the inner good expressed; now they decide the best way to get this person to bring it out.

By telling him he is really good, that we love and value him? Or by being strict, telling him we expect more? It depends on the person and his nature. So you will do whichever it takes: for your real goal, what matters is which works.

blocks.title: Live and let live, or sit down together
blocks.text: One *Tikun* of the *middos* of *Tohu* is like a *reshus harabim* (public domain), something like America: everyone keeps his own will, we only make sure nobody kills those who disagree, and people deal in what does not touch their essential will.

A real *Tikun* means two people actually sit down and work together, by finding a deeper, common goal that transcends both their particulars. In *Tohu*, even coming out, it is only a *sefira*, not a *partzuf*.

phrases.he: ולא פרצוף אדם,
phrases.en: It's not a person.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת ההתכללות מכל ההפכים כו'

blocks.text: Not a *partzuf*: **it's not a person**; you are still talking to a wall. A person is the inclusion of all opposites.

You see this a lot with *baalei teshuva* (returnees to Judaism). Without proper instruction it is very easy for them to end up not being a person. Their whole approach to religion is *emuna*, with a passionate drive for altruism; tied to one aspect of the truth, it makes them forcefully attached to it, and they are not going to be human. There is no sitting down and talking with them: they are on a holy mission, and when you try to talk to them, they are not there.

sensitivity.reason: A generalisation about baalei teshuva: that without proper instruction they easily end up "not human", impossible to talk to.
sensitivity.publishable: You see this a lot. Without proper instruction it is very easy for a person to end up not being a person. If his whole approach to religion is *emuna*, with a passionate drive for altruism, tied to one aspect of the truth, it makes him forcefully attached to it, and he is not going to be human. There is no sitting down and talking with him: he is on a holy mission, and when you try to talk to him, he is not there.

blocks.text: Say something they do not want to hear and they get angry, put you down, even insult you, to invalidate your opinion by invalidating you or the thing itself. They already know it is bad, so any way will do; they are not weighing what you say. It is not healthy, nor comfortable to be around.

sensitivity.reason: Continues the generalisation about baalei teshuva who were not properly instructed.
sensitivity.publishable: Say something he does not want to hear and he gets angry, puts you down, even insults you, to invalidate your opinion by invalidating you or the thing itself. He already knows it is bad, so any way will do; he is not weighing what you say. It is not healthy, nor comfortable to be around.

blocks.text: A person sees a deeper will and how the wills fit, so he sees the other's view: in practice, by a *ratzon murkav*, I may prefer this, but I understand him, and want that too.
As the Baal Shem Tov said, a bad you see in another you have in yourself: every person really has all these wills.

blocks.title: The truth, and the lower realms
blocks.text: People often fight because each locks onto an essential will when inwardly they want the same thing. A *dira b'tachtonim* means bringing the full truth of *Yiddishkeit* down into the lower realms. One locks onto the truth, which cannot be diluted; the other onto its having to be in the lower realms.

It is like one person in the lights and vessels of *Tohu*, another in those of *Tikun*: one drops the real goal to compromise; another keeps his goal but will never reach it, since he will not compromise on how. Some are altruistic but not practical, some practical. Your real goal is to bring it out, so you need both.

phrases.he: אלא בבחינת התיקון, דוקא
phrases.en: the *inyan* of a person is *davka* in a way of *Tikun*,

phrases.he: שכל נקודה בא בהתפשטות חוץ מעצמיותה,
שאז מתכללים על ידי ריבוי הכלים מכלים שונים שמורכבים בהם כו'
phrases.en: when it comes out from the *etzem hanekuda* into *Tikun*, then all the opposite things are expressed, but they're expressed in a limited way, kind of.

phrases.he: ודי למבין

blocks.title: From the yeshiva to mivtzaim
blocks.text: **The *inyan* of a person is *davka* in a way of *Tikun***, every *nekuda* coming out of its essence. You do not leave it in its altruism. A teenager in *yeshiva* can easily be altruistic; on *mivtzaim* you have to be practical. Religion is truly all or nothing: if this is what G-d wants, I will do everything. But you cannot tell that to someone you want to bring closer: no one can start by doing everything.

blocks.text: It is the *mashal* we used for the *igulim*: they are the thing hidden, this is the thing revealed in a particular; the only difference is essence or particular.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: To bring it into *Tikun*, a person does not drop the essential thing: he writes it on a piece of paper and puts it in his pocket, then asks what his practical goal is. If he really wants what *Hashem* wants, a baby step is not hypocritical; it is the only way he will ever get there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: The *yetzer hara* says to do everything, perfectly, or not at all, because it comes from *Tohu*, all or nothing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: The *chesed* of *Tohu* says: my bond with G-d is essential, He will love me whatever I do, so what I do does not matter. That comes out as *kelipa*, the root of the *kelipa* of Yishmael.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: The *gevura* of *Tohu* says that nothing one does will be good enough for G-d, never the *mitzvos* done perfectly or His full glory expressed in action, for "there is no righteous man on earth." And if there is always room to improve, why start?
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: This is the root of the *kelipa* of Esav, a *gevura* of *kelipa*. He knows little of Muslim philosophy, but Christianity says: G-d wants you to do the Torah and the *mitzvos*, but you cannot do them without sinning somewhere, so you need not do any; just rely on being saved by "Yoshke". So out of the *gevura* of *kelipa* came a kind of *chesed*, do whatever you want: they are so *gevura*-dik by nature that they give up.

blocks.text: So the *yetzer hara* makes a person altruistic of a kind, locked into one essential *midda* until it paralyzes him: a *ratzo* without a *shov*, running to *Tohu*, which is good, with no focus on the result.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: Focused on the result, wanting it to come down in practice, you use *chesed* to move you to do good: however low I am, there is some meaningful step I can take, and I have value. G-d treasures him, and his little effort is worth as much to G-d as a great *tzaddik*'s, because it is on his level. So it comes into holiness.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 76 speaks on line 46 from its opening reading of the line's first half (w0-59) until it reads the second half at w1201, where the alignment marks the line.

blocks.text: And *gevura*: however much I have done, there is always room to improve. So Yitzchak and Yaakov used *chesed* and *gevura*. Focused on the bottom line, what you actually accomplish, it is *Tikun*, a good thing; otherwise, *Tohu*.

blocks.text: Then they are revealed in many vessels: **when it comes out from the *etzem hanekuda* into *Tikun*, then all the opposite things are expressed, but they're expressed in a limited way, kind of**. Each finds its place; that is a *partzuf*, all expressed together because each is limited.

phrases.he: וזה מה שכתוב בספר יצירה
טרף אש ומים ובללן זה בזה
phrases.en: Take *eish u'mayim* and mix them together.

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת המורכב דאש ומים דוקא, ולא בעצם מהותן כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות:

blocks.text: So *Sefer Yetzira* says: **Take *eish u'mayim* and mix them together**; that is how *Hashem* made the world. Essential fire and water are opposites, physically and spiritually, but a physical world needed those forms combined: nothing is purely fire or purely water, and so too spiritually.

The composite of fire and water *davka*, not their essence, as explained elsewhere at length. In physical things you never have one without the other: nothing outwardly perfect, nothing without merit.

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that each *sefira* of *Tohu* is a *nekuda*, and why does dividing each *sefira* into ten make *Tikun*?
Why is the person who reads Dale Carnegie's book not *chafetz chesed*, and what does the essential will for kindness have that his will lacks?
Why can two opposite essential wills not compromise, and what happens to the person who is "totally nice, always" or who says "get it yourself"?
Why could Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel not convince each other, and why is their dispute only half an example?
How is kindness to one who saved your life different from the kindness of a person who is kind by nature?
How could G-d punish Shaul and order his eulogy at the same time, and what does that show about the composite *middos* of *Tikun*?

In the verses (Shmuel II 21) the plague is for Shaul's killing of the Givonim; the link to helping Dovid comes through the city of Nov, whose kohanim gave Dovid food and whom the Givonim served (a Midrashic reading). The block keeps his words; a reviewer may want to check.
"Where His judgement is, there..." (74 w1106): he says he forgets the end of the verse; the block keeps it as an unfinished quotation.

"That's the way that Yitzchak and Yaakov used chesed and gevura" (76 w1138-1150): kept as he said it, though chesed and gevura are usually paired with Avraham and Yitzchak. A reviewer may want to check whether he misspoke. The next sentence's "the ratzui of Tikun" (76 w1173-1185) is unclear in the transcript and is rendered only as "it is of Tikun".

"The long short way and the short long way" (73 w1638-1776): he tells it without naming the source; it is the Gemara's story (Eruvin 53b) of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya and a child at a crossroads, which he retells as a way to a palace. Kept as he tells it.

"One person in the lights of Tohu and the vessels of Tohu, one in the lights of Tikun and the vessels of Tikun" (75 w2183-2220): kept as he said it; the pairing with the two people that follow (the one who compromises the goal and the one who will not compromise the means) is not spelled out, and he may have meant lights of Tohu in vessels of Tikun.
